Smart Reads of the Week: Singapore Bank Dividends, Share Buybacks, and Long-Term Stocks
article:
Great investing is not just about finding the next big winner. It is also about knowing which businesses are worth holding, understanding when a dividend is sustainable, and recognising when a seemingly cheap stock may carry more risk than it appears.
This week’s Smart Reads compares DBS, OCBC, and UOB after their latest results, while exploring blue-chip dividend hikes and companies quietly buying back their own shares.
We also look at five stocks built to last, the impact of a bank sell-off on the STI, REIT value, and the warning signs behind unusually high dividend yields.
Here are this week’s top articles:
DBS vs. OCBC vs. UOB: Which Bank Delivered the Best Results and Dividend?
Singapore’s three banking giants have delivered their latest results. We compare their profits, dividends, and overall performance to see which came out on top.
3 SGX Stocks Quietly Buying Back Their Own Shares Recently
Share buybacks can signal management confidence. Here are three companies putting their own cash behind their shares.
5 Stocks I’d Hold Even If the Market Closed for a Decade
Five quality businesses that could reward investors who focus on the underlying companies rather than daily share price movements.
If Singapore Bank Stocks Crash, What Happens to the STI?
With DBS, OCBC, and UOB making up a large part of Singapore’s benchmark, we examine what a major banking sell-off could mean for the STI.
3 Singapore Blue-Chip Stocks That Recently Raised Dividends by 33% and Much More
These blue chips have delivered significant dividend increases. But investors should look beyond the headline percentages to understand what is funding the payouts.
Suntec REIT vs MPACT: Which Offers Better Value for Investors?
We compare two established REITs across valuation, income, and growth potential to see which looks more attractive today.
The Pros and Cons of Investing in Stocks
Stocks can be powerful long-term wealth builders, but understanding their risks is just as important as knowing their potential rewards.
When Yields Explode: 4 Red Flags in Massive Dividend Payouts
A soaring dividend yield may look tempting, but it can sometimes be a warning sign. Here are four red flags investors should watch.
